Incorporating the Beige Book alongside the June 15, 2022 FOMC statement points to a mixed but net negative near‑term outlook. Beige Book contacts indicated tight labor markets with robust employment and widespread wage increases across Districts, with firms even offering more job flexibility to attract/retain workers. Businesses continued to pass through higher input costs (including fuel surcharges), consistent with broad and persistent price pressures. Geopolitical factors (Russia’s invasion of Ukraine) and COVID-related lockdowns in China were adding to cost pressures and supply chain disruptions, with some consumer activity sensitive to COVID waves. Against this inflation backdrop, the Fed’s 75 bp hike and balance-sheet runoff represent a clearly hawkish tightening of financial conditions.

However, credit supply conditions from the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey were more supportive than financial-stability headlines alone imply: domestic banks eased C&I loan standards and reduced credit line costs amid stronger business loan demand (inventories, A/R, capex), multifamily standards eased, and consumer credit standards eased for credit cards with stronger HELOC and auto demand (though RRE softened). This resilience suggests credit was still flowing, partially offsetting the growth drag from policy tightening.

Net assessment: hawkish policy and elevated inflation are a headwind for near-term activity and risk sentiment, but Beige Book/SLOOS resilience makes the outlook less negative than a policy-only read would imply.
